title: When THE PROMOTER meets THE SEMIOLOGIST:
subtitle: The Passion of the Meat

script.text: In the squalid, smoke-filled hall of the Élysée-Montmartre, the air is thick with the smell of sweat and cheap tobacco. Under the harsh, vertical glare of the floodlights—a light without shadow—two figures watch the spectacle.
One is THE PROMOTER (representing Commercial Sport/The Ignoble Spectacle). He chews a cigar and counts the house. To him, wrestling is a business of fake fights for a gullible crowd.

script.speaker: THE Promoter
script.text: Look at them

script.speaker: THE Promoter
script.text: They think it's real. They think Thauvin, that fat slob over there, is really evil. It's a circus for the suburbs. It's fake, but it pays the bills
The other figure is THE SEMIOLOGIST (representing Barthes/Structuralism). He wears a trench coat and watches not the score, but the signs. To him, wrestling is not a sport; it is a ritual.

script.speaker: THE Semiologist
script.text: You are wrong

script.speaker: THE Semiologist
script.text: The public does not think it is real. They do not care if it is rigged. They are here for the Spectacle of Excess. This is not a sport like boxing, where you bet on the future. This is a theatre of the immediate. Each gesture is a word written in flesh
He points to Thauvin, a fifty-year-old wrestler with a sagging, obese body, who is currently biting his opponent's ear.

script.speaker: THE SEMIOLOGIST
script.text: Look at Thauvin

script.speaker: THE Semiologist
script.text: He is not just a man. He is la barbaque—stinking meat. His very flesh signifies baseness. He is the Bastard. When he cheats, the crowd does not boo because they want fair play. They boo because they want the Image of Justice. They want to see the Bastard punished

script.speaker: THE Promoter
script.text: You overthink it. They just want blood

script.speaker: THE Semiologist
script.text: They want Intelligibility. In life, suffering is ambiguous. We suffer for no reason. Justice is delayed. Good and Evil are mixed. But here? Here, every sign is clear. When the wrestler is thrown to the mat, he does not just fall; he exhibits his defeat. He holds the pose like a pause in music. He is crucified in broad daylight
Suddenly, the hero—a clean-cut man with a noble jaw—grabs Thauvin and delivers a "forearm smash" to his chest. Thauvin collapses in a heap of quivering jelly.

script.speaker: THE HERO
script.text: There
cries The Semiologist.

script.speaker: THE SEMIOLOGIST
script.text: The forearm smash! It is the ultimate sign of catastrophe. It is grandiloquent. It is excessive. It is the pure gesture that separates Good from Evil
The crowd roars, "Give it to him! Make him pay!"

script.speaker: THE Semiologist
script.text: See

script.speaker: THE Semiologist
script.text: They demand payment. An eye for an eye. Wrestling is a quantitative sequence of compensations. It is the only place left where Justice is visible
The match ends. Thauvin, the villain, limps away. But a moment later, he walks out of the hall, arm-in-arm with his wife, carrying a small suitcase. He looks normal. Anonymous.

script.speaker: THE MATCH
script.text: The spell is broken

script.speaker: THE Promoter
script.text: Just a job

script.speaker: THE Semiologist
script.text: On the contrary

script.speaker: THE Semiologist
script.text: The transmutation is complete. For twenty minutes, that man was a god. He opened the door to Nature. He showed us a world without ambiguity. And now, he returns to the grey confusion of life, having purified us all
